A three-mana artifact that ramps is fine, but the copy mode needs a good creature already on board and it's gone by end of turn — a hasty one-shot attacker for three. Play it in BR artifacts for the count; otherwise a marginal 23rd card.
Fledgling Dragon: Cut it. Threshold almost never turns on in a format with no self-mill, so you're paying 2RR for a 2/2 flyer — the 47.8% GIH and -5.3 IWD are among the worst in the set, and a 17.5% play rate means most drafters already figured it out. Sideboard.
Laelia, the Blade Reforged: First-pick red rare: 60.9% GIH, 95% play rate, ALSA 1.8. A hasty three-drop that grows every attack and generates card advantage the turn it lands, so it's great on an empty board and great on a stalled one. Everything red wants her; take her over premium removal.
Meltdown: Sideboard card, essentially unplayed at 0.5%. With only 31 artifacts in the set, maindecking a sorcery that hits nothing is a dead slot. Bring it in only against the one drafter at the table on BR artifacts, and only if you saw multiple Cranial Rams go by.
Meteoric Mace: Trap. Six mana for an Equipment that still costs four to move, in a format where the RW and RG decks have won by turn eight — 48.7% GIH with a 13% play rate. Cascade dresses it up but you're paying full price for the dressing. Leave it out.
Annoyed Altisaur: Excellent top end for green ramp — seven mana buys a 6/5 reach trample plus a free spell, and cascade in a set this dense with cheap value rarely misses. 56.8% with a 3.8 ALSA; it's a build-around finisher for GU/RG, so take the ramp first and this will still be there.
Branching Evolution: Hard trap and the worst-performing card in this batch — 43.8% GIH with a −7.6 IWD. Three mana, zero board impact, in a format where the middle loses. Even in BG modified the counter density isn't there (only ~10 cards actually care). Never maindeck it.
Priest of Titania: Filler. Two-mana ramp is exactly what Temur wants, but there are almost no other Elves in MH3, so this is a Llanowar Elves with extra words — and it dies to everything. 54.0% with −0.6 IWD is the profile of a card that's fine on turn two and blank on turn eight. Take the colorless spawn-makers over it if you're the ramp deck.
Sylvan Safekeeper: Niche rare that outperforms its look — 55.9% with a 56.8% OH means it's protecting something on curve. Sacrificing lands to blank removal is real in GU Eldrazi ramp (you have spare lands) and in GW auras (shroud saves the whole investment). Mid-pick in green; the 1/1 body does nothing.
Wirewood Symbiote: Unplayable — there are no Elves. 1.5% play rate and a 47.4% GIH from a tiny sample; it's a 1/1 with a blank ability in this set. Last pick, no exceptions.
Breya, Etherium Shaper: Castable only in a landscape-heavy four-colour pile, which is why the play rate is 30% — but the +8.6 IWD says when it resolves it wins. Don't build toward it; take it as a reward if your mana already stretches. Not a pick to change lanes for.
Kaalia of the Vast: Skip. Three colours across two wedges with a 3.5% play rate and no win-rate sample — the pool basically never supports casting it, and even resolved you need an Angel, Demon, or Dragon in hand. Read is provisional given no data, but a 4-mana 2/2 flier isn't the payoff.
Emerald Medallion: Cut. 3.1% play rate and no meaningful WR sample — a do-nothing two-mana artifact that saves a mana on green spells you may not even have. Not an artifact-count payoff worth the slot even in BR. Sideboard, always.
Jet Medallion: Not a Limited card. Saving one mana on black spells does nothing in a deck running eight or nine black cards, and a 6.2% play rate with 49.4% GIH confirms drafters correctly leave it out. Pass unless you're Constructed-minded.
Junk Diver: Unplayable at 47.4% GIH and a 17.8% play rate. Three mana for a 1/1 flier is off-rate even in BR artifacts, and the death trigger returning an artifact is too slow for a deck that wants Cranial Ram counts on board now. Do not maindeck it.
Pearl Medallion: Unplayable in Limited — 2.6% play rate and no win-rate sample. Two mana that shaves one off white spells does nothing on the turn it lands and does not affect the board; in a format where the middle loses, a do-nothing two-drop is a loss. Never main it.
Ruby Medallion: Cut it — a 4.2% play rate and no meaningful WR sample. Two mana that affects neither the board nor your card count is close to unplayable in Limited, and shaving one off red spells in a format with no red card-advantage engine doesn't pay it back. Read is provisional on the data, but the direction is clear.
Sapphire Medallion: Unplayable in Limited — a do-nothing two-mana artifact that shaves one off blue spells you may not even have enough of. No GIH WR because only 2.4% of decks ran it, which is the whole verdict. Provisional only in that the sample is empty; the read is not in doubt.
Urza's Incubator: Do-not-play. 42.2% GIH and −6.7 IWD: three mana, no body, and a cost reduction that needs four-plus creatures of one type to break even — MH3's tribal density doesn't exist. The 16% who played it lost games for it.
Worn Powerstone: Role-player only in GU Eldrazi ramp, and LoL's C+ is right. Entering tapped means it's turn-four mana for turn five, but two colorless is exactly the pip type the big Eldrazi demand and basics can't provide. 51.8% with flat IWD says it does nothing outside the ramp deck — it's a wheel pick you take once your lane is set.
Barbarian Ring: Marginal at 53.2% with −2.8 IWD and ALSA 8.1 — it wheels, and it should. Painless mana matters in a fast format, and threshold rarely turns on before the game is decided. Run one in a monored-heavy RW deck for reach, never more.
Cephalid Coliseum: Marginal land for UB draw-three only. The threshold ability rarely turns on before the game is decided, the damage is a real cost in an aggressive format, and UB specifically wants a clean two-color mana base. 16% play rate — skip unless you're the control deck.
Deserted Temple: Near-unplayable — 45.9% GIH, 12.4% play, and the untap mode has no target worth untapping in a Limited deck. The one argument is as a colorless source for double-colorless Eldrazi costs, and a landscape does that job while also fixing your real colours.
Nesting Grounds: Marginal, and Ethan's "C" beats Ben's "B-". Moving counters around re-triggers adapt bonuses, which is cute in a fully built BG counters deck — the 8th-place pair. 51.3% GIH and 45.8% play say the colorless land costs you more than the ability returns. Last-card consideration.
Phyrexian Tower: Near-free inclusion in a black deck but not a high pick — 50.9% GIH is bland because the sacrifice mode rarely matters in Limited. It's a colorless source that can tap for {B}{B} to power double-black costs like Breathe Your Last. The -3.5 oh/gd split says it's a land you'd rather draw than open.
Solitude: First pick, no discussion. 62.9% GIH with +8.4 IWD is the best mark in the chunk: free instant-speed exile removal off evoke when you're behind, or a lifelink body when you're ahead. Read is provisional on missing oracle text, but the numbers and ALSA 1.6 leave no ambiguity. Take it over anything.
Subtlety: Solid blue playable, not the bomb LoL called it — 54.8% GIH is mid for a mythic, even at 85.4% play. Read is provisional (no oracle text in this record), but the pattern of an evoke-style free answer is clear: the free mode costs you a card, the hard-cast mode is a fine flash flier. Good pick, not a slam.
Grief: Strong black mythic even without oracle text on this tile, so treat the read as provisional: 59.1% GIH at 84.9% play rate and a 2.0 ALSA is the profile of a cheap, aggressive body with disruption stapled on. High pick for any black deck, though not the game-ender Phlage is.
Fury: Bomb — P1P1 over almost anything. 64.4% GIH with the set's best IWD (+10.5) and ALSA 1.5 means every table takes it immediately and it wins the games it's in. The free-evoke mode is a two-for-one that breaks open the RW and RG go-wide boards this format is built around; hard-cast it late as a double-strike finisher.
Endurance: Provisional read — no oracle text or cost in the record. A three-mana 3/4 reach flash Elemental Incarnation with a graveyard-hate ETB and a free evoke; in MH3 Limited that's a fine flash blocker but not a bomb, and the 53.0% with a -1.4 IWD confirms it underperforms its constructed reputation.
Thought-Knot Seer: Solid colorless beater with disruption attached — read is provisional (no oracle text in the record), but the 4/4 body plus hand attack for four is the known package. 85% play rate at 55.2% means every deck with a {C} source plays it; the colorless pip is the real constraint, so have landscapes or spawns.
Prismatic Ending: No oracle text or live WR in the record, so this read is provisional — but the card is a scaling X-mana exile that answers any nonland permanent of low mana value, which in a Limited pool is most of them. The 4.1 ALSA and 37% play rate suggest it was contested but only cast in decks with real fixing. Treat as premium white removal when you can pay multiple colors.
Dismember: Premium removal and a first pick regardless of colors — 59.5% GIH with a 95.5% play rate and ALSA 1.7, the best combined profile in this chunk. Its record has no oracle text so this read is provisional, but the numbers are unambiguous: cheap, effectively colorless interaction that every deck plays.
Persist: Provisional — no oracle text in the record, but a cheap black reanimation sorcery is only as good as the best creature in your yard, and 51.3% GIH with a 3.0 ALSA shows drafters taking it on rarity and getting replacement-level results. Playable in BG/BR grind, not a first pick.
Expressive Iteration: Card advantage for the Jeskai wedge, not a bomb. Oracle text is missing from the record, so this is read from the known card — exile three, play a land and a spell — and +4.7 IWD at 57.8% play matches that. Remember UR itself finished 9th; this card is better than its archetype.
Disa the Restless: Provisional — the record has no text or cost. Colour identity spans BRG, which means two wedges, and the 52.6% GIH with a 3.3 ALSA says drafters took it early and it underperformed. Treat a three-colour mythic here as a splash-only card; the wedges share almost nothing.
Omo, Queen of Vesuva: Provisional read — no oracle text in the record — but the numbers are clear enough: 47.7% GIH and a 29.1% play rate on a GU mythic means the card doesn't do enough fast enough. Temur wants ramp and Eldrazi bodies, not a five-mana legend that doesn't affect the board. Low pick.
Satya, Aetherflux Genius: Jeskai bomb and a first-pick that also tells you your lane. 62.5% GIH with a +9.0 IWD is near-Solitude territory, and the 62.3% opening-hand WR means it wins games from any point in the curve. Text is missing from this record, so the read is provisional — but three colors in the format's best wedge is a green light, not a cost.
Ulalek, Fused Atrocity: Hard trap and the worst card here: 44.3% GIH with −6.7 IWD, yet still maindecked 60% of the time — drafters keep trying and keep losing. Read is provisional without text, but a five-colour legendary Eldrazi in a format where pivoting is near-impossible cannot be cast. Leave it in the sideboard.
Azlask, the Swelling Scourge: The clearest trap in this chunk. A five-color legendary Eldrazi posted 47.2% at a 17.3% play rate — even the drafters who cast it lost with it, and the mana cost is unmeetable outside a spawn-flooded Temur board. Read is provisional without text, but the numbers are damning. Do not play it.
Cayth, Famed Mechanist: Mediocre for a mythic — 54.0% GIH and only 64% play rate, because three colours across two wedges is a genuinely hard cast in a format where pivoting is punished. Playable if you're already Jeskai with fixing; otherwise it sits in the pool. Read is provisional (no oracle text in the record), but the numbers are mature and unflattering.
Coram, the Undertaker: Provisional — no text in the record, and the numbers already say skip. A Jund-costed legend at 50.0% with a -2.9 IWD is asking you to play three colours across two wedges, which the doctrine flags as the known 1-3 pile. Take the mono-coloured card instead.
Jyoti, Moag Ancient: Provisional — no win-rate data and a 2.3% play rate, so almost nobody has cast it. As a GU legend it points at Temur ramp, which is the wedge that can actually pay for a gold mythic. Treat it as an untested top-end pick, not a known quantity.
